details: app-use republishes an existing macOS desktop-automation command-line tool under a new name; its JavaScript launcher was changed to also run an included Linux x86-64 binary that is not part of the original tool. On Linux, every invocation of the `application-use` command (including `--help`) runs that binary, which unconditionally starts a hidden shell command and does nothing else; there is no preinstall, install or postinstall script, so nothing runs on `npm install` or import. The command sends data in plaintext to qdore.top:8484: /opt/hatch/bin/hatch in the earlier working versions (0.2.1 to 0.2.4), and in 0.3.0 a tar archive of /opt/hatch-private/prompts written to /tmp/p.tar. The targeted paths are not standard user-data locations; their names suggest they may correspond to the cloud VM environment of Meta's Muse agent, though this has not been confirmed. Remediation: uninstall the package, block qdore.top, check hosts that ran it for /tmp/p.tar and nohup.out, and treat the contents of /opt/hatch and /opt/hatch-private on those hosts as disclosed.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
